items.title: Hideo Kojima Says You'll See Him Cameo in a 'Big' Live-Action Movie — But Which One Is It?
items.excerpt: Hideo Kojima teased that he's got a cameo in a "big" live-action movie, but he's not saying which one we'll see him in quite yet.
items.content_text: Hideo Kojima teased that he's got a cameo in a "big" live-action movie, but he's not saying which one we'll see him in quite yet. The Metal Gear Solid and Death Stranding creator enticed film fans to theorize about his movie career during a surprise installment in the Koji10 podcast . In between talking about Physint and what's next for his Kojima Productions, the famed game developer revealed that he would appear in movie theaters as part of a big new live-action movie cameo. "I already shot a few other things," Kojima said, as translated through YouTube's English captions (via @Genki_JPN ). "Directors and others have asked me to." The topic came up when reminiscing about his time doing voice acting work as a mole in Zootopia 2 . While the Japanese version of the Pixar film had him provide his talents behind the scenes, he suggested this mysterious new project will allow him to be in front of the camera in some capacity. So as not to spoil the surprise, he said he "can't say" what it is yet, but it is a "big movie." It is indeed live-action, too, but his involvement is so secretive for now that he even refused to tell his hosts where he shot his part. Kojima is best known for his work as a game developer, but he's also a well-read cinephile, too. Fans routinely turn up for his reviews of movies like Superman , Backrooms , Spider-Man: Brand New Day , and more. Even his social media biography jokes that "70% of my body is made of movies," so it's no surprise to see him continue to be as involved in film as he can manage. Many have also already started speculating when exactly we'll see Kojima show up, too, even if no one has any truly solid leads to go on yet. Some have guessed we'll see him in Denis Villeneuve's Dune: Part 3 this December, while others suggested he'll show up in The Legend of Zelda movie , or even next month's Godzilla Minus Zero . Other guesses come from those who are just happy to see their favorite game creator show up in live-action at all. "Hideo Kojima will return in Avengers: Doomsday," one fan said . Kojima also said his future in entertainment will see him in not one but two "major anime" titles. These are "really big" but still a mystery for audiences for now, with the developer only saying that he has speaking lines coming up. He also said that an upcoming game cameo – a concept that is far from new for him – is also a secret, though fans have already found evidence that he's been scanned for Naughty Dog's Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet . In terms of Kojima's main occupation, he's still very much at work on his new espionage action game, Physint. He offered an update on the Bill Skarsgård-starring title's progress during today's podcast, too, teasing that many of the characters' names have already been decided, and their actors scanned. He's also still heads-down working on his horror game, OD . Photo by Rosdiana Ciaravolo/Getty Images.

items.content_text: Ahead of Prime Big Deal Days, Amazon has brought back its popular "3 for 2" book sale . A notable inclusion for Brandon Sanderson fans is the sci-fi author's latest book, Blightfall, which marks the start of Riftwake — a new series and the first official expansion to the Cytoverse. Blightfall is less than $2 off on its own, so this sale is only really worth it if you can find two more books you'd want to pair with it. I'd recommend checking out Sanderson's Cosmere universe books, which are also included in the promotion as well. Amazon '3 for 2' Sale on Brandon Sanderson Books Brandon Sanderson's Cytoverse is still fairly new. The universe was kicked off by the Skyward series, which focused on building a sci-fi world more grounded in the YA genre . During IGN's interview , Sanderson explained his intention to skew a tad younger with his writing "because the story is about teens who are forced, before their time, into leadership roles on a planet where war has claimed the lives of much of the older population." Although the Skyward series technically "started" the universe, you don't actually need to read it to jump into Blightfall. Similar to the Cosmere books , this series acts as a new entry point rather than a sequel. That being said, I do highly recommend checking out Skyward as it's actually a terrific original sci-fi fantasy story. Plus there's already a TV series in the works for it. items.title: Ubisoft Boss Says Watch Dogs Is 'Important' to Company's Future, But Don't Expect Any New Entries Anytime Soon
items.excerpt: Don't hold your breath for a new Watch Dogs game anytime soon.
items.content_text: Don't hold your breath for a new Watch Dogs game anytime soon. As reported by Game File , Ubisoft CEO Yves Guillemot was asked by an investor about the future of the Watch Dogs franchise. The CEO noted that Ubisoft considers the IP "to be an important brand for the future" but neglected to explain how. Game File's Stephen Totilo stated that Guillemot suggested that there are no Watch Dogs games in active development at the moment, which suggests Ubisoft may still be figuring out where to take the series from here. There is a Watch Dogs movie on the horizon , but there's no word on when it will be released. The film wrapped production two years ago and had reshoots last year, but there hasn't been any sort of meaningful promotion for the film to date. As of right now, it doesn't even have a release date, which makes it even more of a mystery. Watch Dogs made its debut back in 2014, though it was initially meant to launch simultaneously with the PS4 in November 2013. Ubisoft hyped it up as a direct competitor to Grand Theft Auto 5, which released in September 2013. Unfortunately, many felt it was unable to reach some of its ambitions, but it still managed to make a dent in the open-world crime genre. Two years later, Ubisoft launched a much more impressive sequel set in San Francisco, but failed to keep the momentum going with its third installment. Watch Dogs: Legion was released in 2020, also boasting ambitious ideas, such as the ability to control any NPC in the world. Unfortunately, the game received generally mixed reception from fans. Since then, there have been a lot of question marks around the future of the franchise. It seems Ubisoft wants to do more with Watch Dogs, but it may be trying to figure out how it can separate itself from a game like Grand Theft Auto 6 , which is set to shake up the genre in November. There may be more Watch Dogs games one day, but don't expect them within the next few years.
items.title_en: Ubisoft Boss Says Watch Dogs Is 'Important' to Company's Future, But Don't Expect Any New Entries Anytime Soon

items.title: Miami Vice: The Final Director’s Cut’s Ending Invites a Darker Reading of Michael Mann’s Cult Classic
items.excerpt: Miami Vice: The Director’s Final Cut’s rejiggered ending invites a slightly darker interpretation of the film than was evident in either of the past versions, especially when considered with what writer-director Michael Mann revealed about the fact-based origins of his screenplay at the post-premiere Q&A.
items.content_text: Full SPOILERS follow for all three versions of Michael Mann’s Miami Vice movie. Miami Vice: The Director’s Final Cut premiered at Beyond Fest on Saturday. With the exception of the reordering of a few moments at the very end — and the omission of Nonpoint’s cover of “In the Air Tonight” — this version is largely the same as the Unrated Director’s Edition that was released on Blu-ray years ago. But the Final Cut’s rejiggered ending is enough to invite a slightly darker interpretation of the story than was evident in either of the film’s past versions, especially when considered with what writer-director Michael Mann revealed about the fact-based origins of his screenplay at the post-premiere Q&A. Mann’s film version of the iconic 1980s TV series , which he executive produced but did not create, has been a love it or hate it affair since it came out in 2006. If you haven’t seen the Unrated Director’s Edition and are only familiar with the theatrical cut , then you will find much to unpack with this Director’s Final Cut when it arrives on 4K UHD and Blu-ray on December 15. All three versions of Mann’s Miami Vice follow Miami-Dade P.D. undercover detectives James "Sonny" Crockett (a gruff, mustachioed Colin Farrell) and Ricardo Tubbs (a no-nonsense Jamie Foxx), who are recruited to infiltrate a Latin American narco-trafficking network after a mole has been discovered inside a joint Federal task force. Crockett and Tubbs sneak into South America by air and, once there, meet with sinister middleman Jose Yero (a scene-stealing John Ortiz). They succeed in insinuating themselves into Yero and his boss Montoya’s operation. Crockett also falls for Isabella (Gong Li), a businesswoman who serves as the financial brains of Montoya’s operation. Crockett romances Isabella in the hopes of acquiring information (and she from him) but they soon genuinely fall for each other. It is not meant to be. She discovers during the climactic shootout that "Sonny Burnett" is actually cop Sonny Crockett. But Crockett can’t bring himself to arrest Isabella, instead arranging for her to escape via boat and start her life over elsewhere. All of that remains in the Final Cut, but the use of the song “In the Air Tonight,” the scene of Montoya’s empty compound being raided, and the very last shot of Crockett returning to the hospital where wounded fellow detective Trudy Joplin (Naomie Harris) is have all been removed in this version. "The viewer is left to wonder what Crockett does next after letting a key player in their undercover operation escape justice. Mann’s Miami Vice was a legendarily difficult production, culminating in the abrupt departure of Jamie Foxx, who abandoned the film during shooting in the Dominican Republic, a move that forced Mann to change the movie’s ending . Mann never shot what he needed to end the story as he had originally envisioned. Both the theatrical cut and the earlier Unrated Director’s Edition end with Crockett returning to the hospital where badly injured Vice cop Trudy, comforted by Tubbs, emerges from her coma. Although he let Isabella escape, Crockett ultimately returns to his police family in both previous versions. Closing those versions with a shot of Crockett walking into the hospital always made for an awkward ending, but it communicated that Crockett ultimately remembers whose side he’s on. But the Director’s Final Cut instead ends with Crockett walking back to his car while Isabella flees before cutting to the end credits. The viewer is left to wonder what Crockett does next after letting a key player in their undercover operation escape justice. Mann’s revision of those closing moments suggests a reading of the film where Crockett’s future is uncertain. In the Beyond Fest post-screening Q&A, Mann shed light on his reasons for revising the ending and why he wanted to refocus the ending of his Final Cut of Miami Vice on Crockett and Isabella’s love story. Mann also revealed that the tragic inspiration for his screenplay was an undercover agent he was acquainted with: “I knew a number of people, one guy in particular who did very, very difficult long-term undercover in foreign countries – Beirut, Marseilles, Hong Kong. And I became fascinated with the dynamics of what happened when you lived a fabricated identity, but the fabricated identity in many cases becomes facets of yourself and it becomes performance, but there's only one take. You cannot make a mistake.” Mann continued: “This was very much based on this one guy who had a family in Florida, wife and kids, and he was undercover working a money laundering operation based out of Hong Kong and fell in love with his target's sister. And if you met the targets, they didn't self-identify as part of a criminal subculture. They just were dealing in commodities. The commodity could be number three opium, it could be tapioca futures. It didn't matter. They were just people of commerce. And it turned his life upside down. It was a long-term relationship. And he was eventually indicted in Florida. And when he realized that he was going to get convicted, they would've seized his real family's assets under RICO. And he went out on I-80 and walked in front of an 18-wheeler.” (Mann said this was the inspiration for how John Hawkes’ informant character commits suicide early in the film.) "When they score and they become very good in this criminal fabricated identity, it is truly like a drug. “These (undercover agents) are very often men and women [who] are projecting the part of themselves that has not been manifested. So it's maybe part of themselves that they suppressed or it's been repressed,” Mann said. “They're convincing somebody that they could handle their transport or that this deal should go down and they sell and they're really good at it because oftentimes they're smarter [than the perps]. “And when they score and they become very good in this criminal fabricated identity, it is truly like a drug,” Mann said of how these agents can, in the parlance of Miami Vice, lose sight of which way is up. In that sense, Crockett’s undercover persona “Sonny Burnett” is so convincing – he is able to seduce Isabella and eventually get her to agree to renegotiating his and Rico’s deal for a new percentage – that the character, in my estimation, begins behaving like an addict whose drug habit is worsening the longer he’s undercover. By the time the film’s final showdown comes along, Sonny is essentially a junkie in freefall. “There often becomes a situation where (the undercover agents) don't go through red lights. There are no red lights. There's no red lights, no yellow lights, no green lights. There are no lights,” said Mann. “Maybe you look in a mirror in the morning when he wakes up and the guy will say that he is truly himself for the first time in his life. “And particularly when you do what you're not supposed to do. They always say you're not supposed to have romances and bullshit. They wind up having romances. And that's basically, that's the genesis of this whole picture.” Crockett’s romance with Isabella certainly doesn’t go unnoticed by his colleagues Rico, Trudy and Gina. While the latter two exchange looks of concern during a sequence at Yero’s club, Tubbs is far more direct with his partner. Tubbs’ concern is evident the minute Crockett ditches him for a boat ride to Havana with Isabella. Crockett assures Tubbs he’s got things under control at several points, but by the time they’re prepping their weapons for the final showdown he admits to Tubbs that he’s “with her 100%.” Tubbs cautions Crockett that Isabella is “with them,” but Sonny is not ready for the collapse of his undercover identity where he will be required to bust the woman he loves. Like an addict struggling with their problem, Crockett assures those around him that he has his issues in check even as his actions and behavior indicate otherwise. His addiction eventually consumes him to the point where he can no longer do the job he’s required to do. The original theatrical and the Unrated versions’ endings suggest Sonny found his way back from that dark place by returning to his Miami Vice colleagues – that he remembers which way is up. Cutting that final shot of Sonny returning to his cop teammates seems like a relatively minor edit, but it’s one where Crockett’s self-destructive behavior and the loss of Isabella carries more thematic weight. He’s lost her, betrayed his badge by not arresting her, and is alone. It’s a more emotional and thought-provoking finale than what the previous two cuts of the film conveyed. Miami Vice: The Director’s Final Cut is available on 4K UHD and Blu-ray on December 15.
items.title_en: Miami Vice: The Final Director’s Cut’s Ending Invites a Darker Reading of Michael Mann’s Cult Classic

items.title: Infinity Ward Details Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's Extraction Mode, DMZ
items.excerpt: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's ambitious new extraction mode, DMZ, has gotten a massive deep dive from Infinity Ward.
items.content_text: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's ambitious new extraction mode, DMZ, has received a massive deep dive from Infinity Ward. DMZ was initially introduced in 2022's Modern Warfare II, and now, with the rise in popularity of extraction shooters, it is coming back in a bigger way . The mode is expected to be a major part of Modern Warfare 4's offerings, with its own 70-level progression system, lucrative rewards, and world building/lore. Additionally, there will be a forward operating base for players to hang out in between matches. Here, players can practice at a firing range to test their loadouts, craft items based on loot they've found in the world, gain intel and track different missions, bosses, and unique challenges for their next deployment, and more. Speaking in a new behind-the-scenes video, Infinity Ward co-studio head Jack O'Hara stated that fans made it clear that there weren't high enough stakes in the first iteration of DMZ, so they've worked to change that. For starters, your time in DMZ is defined by your operator. This is a character that you build and level up, but if they die, it will cost you to bring them back. There are also lootable items that can be permanently lost if the player dies or drops them. These items can be used at a 3D printer to craft things like armor plates, consumables, gear, and seemingly killstreaks or AI-controlled fire support, based on a menu seen in some gameplay. The team behind DMZ also described it as an "action extraction shooter." Infinity Ward wants players to feel like there is constant danger both through AI combatants, bosses, and other players, so you won't spend a ton of time wandering around opening boxes with minimal friction. Infinity Ward laid out a plethora of different enemy types in a blog post , noting that there will be drones, helicopter and vehicle patrols, tanks, and tougher enemies. Different parts of the map will have different threat levels, and those levels can rise based on the player's actions. If you're running around causing a bunch of noise, it will create more attention and lead to enemies searching for you. However, if you play stealtihly with silenced weapons, melee takedowns, and exercise caution, you can avoid extreme conflict. Additionally, the more players explore, the more opportunities there will be to uncover loot and secrets in the game's world. Infinity Ward has also promised extensive support for DMZ post-launch, including changes to the map, dynamic weather that can vary per season, and much more. It sounds like a big focus for the team and it should be a really cool change for Call of Duty. Hopefully it sticks and isn't dropped next year, but that will likely depend on if players show up to support it. DMZ will be available at launch when Modern Warfare 4 releases on October 23. Unlike MWII's version, it will not be free-to-play.

items.title: RuneScape Dev Pulls Trailer After 6-Fingered Knight Leads to Generative AI Allegations
items.excerpt: RuneScape developer Jagex has pulled a new trailer after a six-fingered knight led to allegations of generative AI use from fans.
items.content_text: RuneScape developer Jagex has pulled a new trailer after a six-fingered knight led to allegations of generative AI usage from fans. There were some ups and downs for RuneScape players over the weekend. What started with a string of big reveals from RuneFest 2026 ended with social media users voicing their concern that generative AI had been used to make the new trailer for RuneScape 3 's Dragon Slayer 2 quest. The backlash was loud enough that Jagex stepped in not only to release an official response on the matter but also to pull the trailer entirely while it investigates "urgently." The statement, posted on Reddit by social media manager Alex Sween (via Kotaku ), acknowledged some of the more undeniable concerns related to the trailer – including the fact that one of its knights has six fingers. Jagex using AI for RS3 Dragon Slayer 2 reveal trailer by u/Ok-Ladder4467 in LivestreamFail "Hello, it’s me, again, talking about Gen AI, again," the statement began, referencing a separate, recent incident involving 100 Thieves and OSRS . The team also took a "hard line stance" against generative AI earlier this year. "We’re aware of the concerns raised about the Dragon Slayer 2 trailer and have taken it down, while we investigate urgently. This trailer was produced by a trusted external partner who had explicitly confirmed that GenAI would not be used. But, among other things, there’s a sixth finger and, well, that’s pretty hard to explain away. For that we apologise. Although uploads of RuneScape's Dragon Slayer 2 trailer can no longer be found on official channels, it is still available via the full RuneFest 2026 livestream . There are also plenty of posts from fans discussing the matter still live across social media. They're not happy, but Jagex knows that. The team took its statement and apology as an opportunity to, again, make its position clear: "We don't use GenAI to create our games, artwork, or creative assets and will not knowingly allow it to be used on our behalf." However, it's hard to deny that a second instance of artificial intelligence being used to generate content suggests a deeper problem for the MMO developer. Jagex explained that it plans to address its approach to working with partners going forward. Then today, Jagex decided to use AI in a trailer for an upcoming quest, the knight in video has 6 fingers and boots in a another frame look like modern sneakers. https://t.co/L6w4yotJw0 https://t.co/C9kMM2oC7c — TheNoobishDad (@ABNreaper) October 4, 2026 "Immediately following RuneFest we’re overhauling our review processes," the statement continued, "and we’re going to work with and commission creators from the community to make sure that the story of Dragon Slayer 2 is told to the standard befitting of such an update." The six-fingered knight really does feel like the smoking gun, but another bizarre piece of art from the trailer, which showed a fully-armored knight wearing what seemed to be a regular old pair of tennis shoes, had fans raising eyebrows, too. In follow-up replies, Sween acknowledged it's something Jagex "should have caught," adding, "We didn't do well enough and can't simply place the blame elsewhere." As Jagex refines its processes to maintain its stance against generative AI, it's still working to deliver other new projects. RuneScape 4 is one of these new projects, with an animated adaptation also in the works with YouTuber MoistCr1tikal.

items.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Hot Springs Scenes Reveal New Bathing Suit Skins for the Party
items.excerpt: New Final Fantasy 7 Revelation footage has revealed a hot springs feature that boosts the party's health and gives them a set of new bathing suit skins.
items.content_text: New Final Fantasy 7 Revelation footage has revealed a hot springs feature that boosts the party's health and gives them a set of new bathing suit skins. Half the fun of Square Enix's remake trilogy is allowing Cloud, Barret, Tifa, and the rest of the party to have some fun on their way to stop Sephiroth once and for all. In Rebirth , that meant spending a day at the beach , and in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, players will be able to kick their feet up, mingle, and, for some reason, balance rubber Chocobos at a collection of new hot springs. The publisher unveiled the new gameplay feature as part of SDCC Málaga and later shared gameplay footage on social media. When the group stops at a hot spring, they'll benefit from a permanent increase to their max HP. The health bonus and moments shared between each character seem to be the real draw. The thing that might appeal to some players more than others, though, is the promise that the bathing suit outfits featured during these segments can be unlocked as skins, too. 【名湯めぐりの旅🐤】 冒険の合間に、ほっとひと息。 #FF7リベレーション のワールドマップに隠された温泉スポット♨旅の仲間たちとのここでしか聞けない特別な会話が楽しめます。さらに最大HPアップの効果や衣装スキンが手に入ることも https://t.co/S41hqabFqp — ファイナルファンタジーVII リメイク (@FFVIIR_CLOUD) October 5, 2026 Across all of the clips shown online today, we can see skins for Cloud, Barret, and Cid. Red XIII can relax in the hot springs, too, but considering he's not usually wearing clothes to begin with, it doesn't look like any skin he may get will change his appearance too much. Then, there's newly playable party member Vincent Valentine, who prefers to bathe in the same slick get-up he fights monsters in because he's… just that cool, I guess. "We’re sharing a preview of some of the hot spring events revealed during our stage presentation at SDCC Málaga," director Naoki Hamaguchi said in a follow-up post on X/Twitter. "Each hot spring offers a different glimpse into the characters’ everyday lives, and the outfits featured in these events can also be unlocked as skins. Explore the world, discover hot springs, and enjoy these special moments with your companions!" Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is still months from delivering the concluding chapter of the remake trilogy, but that hasn't stopped Square Enix from unloading new details as often as it can manage. Hamaguchi has been especially keen to share, telling IGN last month that players will have an option to automatically level up their characters if they want to skip the grind. He's also said players could easily spend more than 100 hours playing through the story , even if the Platinum Trophy doesn't present much of a challenge on its own . Final Fantasy 7 Revelation launches for PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S April 8, 2027. While we wait to see how those hot springs heat things up for Cloud and company, you can see how Hamaguchi responded to players hoping for a full-disc release . You can also check out IGN's hands-on preview .

items.title: Physint Update: Hideo Kojima Shares New Info on His Upcoming Metal Gear Spiritual Successor
items.excerpt: Renowned game director Hideo Kojima revived his Koji10 podcast after a year and shared casting, story, and development updates on Physint, his upcoming next-generation action-espionage game and spiritual successor to Metal Gear Solid.
items.content_text: Renowned game director Hideo Kojima revived his Koji10 podcast after a year and shared casting, story, and development updates on Physint, his upcoming next-generation action-espionage game and spiritual successor to Metal Gear Solid. Thanks to a summary of the 79-minute English-subtitled podcast on YouTube by X user Genki_JPN, we now know a bit more about the status of Physint, which made huge headlines recently after Kojima revealed that Sony was set to cancel the project as its publisher, leading to Microsoft picking it up . Kojima describes Physint as a project to commemorate his 40th anniversary as a game developer. He said he wants it to evoke the roots of the Metal Gear Solid games, but be a new interactive experience with a different kind of spy action. He aims to fill it with lots of new ideas. Story and cast-wise, Kojima says he has the plot already and that he pitched all of the actors appearing in it himself – 70% of whom are apparently Kojima fans. Many of the character names have been decided Filming will start next year, with Bill Skarsgard , Charlie Fraser and Minami Hamabe already scanned. Finally, the 63-year-old Kojima said that he makes every one of his games as if it could be his last. The other game Kojima is developing for Microsoft, the PT spiritual successor OD, is expected to be released before Physint, which Kojima himself said was 5-6 years away last year.
